acceptance.criterion: Migrate schema1/2/3 fixture DBs twice; facts, subscriptions, tokens and usage retained; future schema refused without writes; fresh DB and upgraded DB equivalent.
acceptance.expected: A new forward-only migration exists (needed by tasks44/47/48/50) and this round-trip test passes against it.
acceptance.observed: No new migration added. The operations-table design that would need one (proposed decision 2) is not yet chief-architect approved, and 'no worker chooses a weaker substitute' / 'schema owner cannot invent a hidden overage allowance' rules out adding it unreviewed. The existing schema1-3 migration path is unchanged and its own existing round-trip test (store_test.go TestMigrationAndRollback) still passes as part of the scoped verification run below, confirming no regression -- but there is no new migration for this criterion to exercise.

acceptance.criterion: Existing hosted tests and file-first gate pass.
acceptance.expected: go test -race -count=1 ./internal/hosted/store ./internal/hosted/service ./internal/hosted/contracts ./internal/hosted/testhooks ./internal/gate exits 0 with no unexplained skips.
acceptance.observed: Ran exactly that command (GOFLAGS=-p=2, under the held R-build-lease, SHA 9d0099e77ebb0aab98145d650a2317d6fc10d39f, released clean after). 21 test functions passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped, across store/service/testhooks/gate (testhooks grew from 5 to 7 test functions this pass, adding a -race concurrent regression test and an arm-pipe-EOF test for the dispatcher-goroutine fix); contracts has no named tests (compile-time conformance assertions only, verified separately below). go vet and golangci-lint clean on both the plain and hostedtest-tagged build of internal/hosted/testhooks and internal/hosted/contracts.

acceptance.criterion: Interface document lists owning task, exact signature, semantic contract, schema version and integration file for every shared seam.
acceptance.expected: Every row in interfaces.md's seam table has a frozen Go signature, contract and integration file.
acceptance.observed: 9 of 13 seams (billing truth, billing closure, backup manifest v2, recovery CLI shape, telemetry, provider pin, accounting units, registration mode) are frozen with real compiled/tested Go types in internal/hosted/contracts and internal/hosted/testhooks, each proven by a compile-time conformance test (spot-checked red->green by mutating one interface signature and confirming go vet fails, then restoring). The remaining 4 seams tied to the unapproved decisions (operation accounting, storage admission, deletion journal, recovery activation barrier) have revised draft Go signatures in contracts/ marked PROPOSED -- operations.go now carries a Deltas slice instead of a single metric/unit pair plus CanonicalRef and LeaseExpiresAt fields, deletion.go now uses a control-DB SequenceID/Generation watermark instead of an S3 continuation token, and storage.go now proposes measured (not predicted) growth admission -- but still no schema version, since no migration was added pending review.

limitations: Ajent MCP tools (ajent_inbox/ajent_search/ajent_diagnose) require interactive permission grant unavailable in this headless session; coordination was cross-checked against ajent.social directly instead, per AGENTS.md fallback guidance.

No chief-architect review obtained; all four bounded design decisions remain PROPOSED, not approved. An independent review found and this revision fixed concrete defects in three of the four proposed mechanisms (operation accounting, deletion journal watermark, restore fencing) plus the storage admission formula and a testhooks concurrency bug -- see T23.41-review.md and interfaces.md's revision notes.
No schema migration added this pass; store/migrations.go is unchanged.
internal/hosted/service/service.go and internal/cli/hosted.go were read but not edited -- no feature implementation exists yet to wire, and adding no-op registrations was explicitly disallowed.
gateway.go's global map-lock-across-Pool.Acquire violation is documented in interfaces.md's lock-ordering section but not fixed (out of task41's write scope, owned by task45/R-hosted-runtime).

Exact numeric values (measured-growth headroom bytes, operator headroom bytes, retention window) are explicitly left unset in the proposals -- they require either empirical fixture evidence (task44) or an operator/cost decision (task60/61), not a worker guess. Storage admission (decision 1) has no adopted mechanism at all and is explicitly BLOCKED, not merely unset.
